nodes.description: Connexin 26 gap junctions among cochlear supporting cells are required for potassium removal and recycling. Dominant BPS alleles are presumed to impair this network, but the only BPS-specific data come from cochlear-derived HEI-OC1 cells, in which p.Asn54Lys showed trafficking defects yet still formed gap junctions with connexin 30. This node does not declare conforms_to on sensorineural_hair_cell_loss because that module's ionic homeostasis node also asserts increased oxidative stress and a hair-cell death step for which there is no BPS evidence.

evidence.reference_title: The role of connexins in ear and skin physiology - functional insights from disease-associated mutations.
evidence.snippet: These approaches have provided evidence supporting a role of gap junctions and hemichannels in K(+) removal and recycling in the ear, as well as possible roles for nutrient passage, in the cochlea.

evidence.reference_title: GJB2 Mutations Linked to Hearing Loss Exhibit Differential Trafficking and Functional Defects as Revealed in Cochlear-Relevant Cells.
evidence.snippet: GJB2 gene (that encodes Cx26) mutations are causal of hearing loss highlighting the importance of Cx26-based channel signaling amongst the supporting cells in the organ of Corti.

nodes.description: The p.Asn54Lys connexin 26 is retained in an endoplasmic reticulum-like intracellular compartment and forms few gap junction plaques, so channels capable of dye transfer are essentially absent in cells expressing the mutant alone. In lesional palmar and knuckle skin of the index BPS family, connexin 26 immunostaining was weak or absent.
